Server Objects

Browse and maintain a FortiWeb's Server Objects (virtual servers, pools, health checks, certificates, ciphers, allow lists, IP groups and more) on the pages of the device's own Server Objects menu, drawn in FortiWeb's layout.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view network.edit network.apply operations.template_save
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → FortiWeb → Server Objects → <group> → <page> (URL /workspace/<id>/fwgui/<page>; the old /server-objects/<id>?type=<object type> redirects there)

What is it?#

Server Objects is a group of the FortiWeb device menu: the Server Objects menu of the appliance's own GUI, measured on the selected device's firmware build. It holds the objects a FortiWeb uses to publish and balance applications — virtual servers, server pools, health checks, certificates, cipher lists, allow lists, IP groups and so on. Each entry opens a page drawn in FortiWeb's layout (its tabs, toolbar and columns) inside the SATOM frame, with SATOM's tools added, and each object opens in FortiWeb's own dialog.

What does it do?#

  • Draws FortiWeb's Server Objects menu under the FortiWeb group of the sidebar, in FortiWeb's order, with the pages the device's build has. All pages shows the same menu as a grid.
  • Shows the entries that FortiWeb draws as tabs of one page (for example Local | Multi-certificate) as tabs above the list.
  • Lists the objects of the selected tab with FortiWeb's columns, a Search box and an object count. Rows come from SATOM's cache of the device; a badge says when the cache was taken, and ⟳ pulls the live configuration. FortiWeb's predefined entries are read live from the device, carry a live badge and are read-only.
  • Opens an object in FortiWeb's dialog (Edit, or View when you cannot write) and creates objects from FortiWeb's Create New menu. Where FortiWeb's layout has no Create New but SATOM can create the object, a Create New button opens the object editor instead.
  • Clone copies the selected object under a new name with its sub-table rows; Delete removes it. Both show a dry run first.
  • For certificate stores that the FortiWeb REST API cannot create, adds Import (and, on Local, Generate).
  • Save as template files the selected object in the Template Library as a pending template, and the config template library of its object type is listed under the table.

The menu holds only the pages the device's build has. On FortiWeb 7.6.8 it is:

Group Pages (tabs)
Server Virtual Server, Server Pool, Health Check, Persistence, HTTP Content Routing
Protected Hostnames Protected Hostnames
Service Service (Predefined, Custom)
Traffic Mirror Traffic Mirror
Certificates Local (Local, Multi-certificate), Let's Encrypt, XML Certificate (Server Certificate, Client Certificate, Client Certificate Group), URL Certificate, SNI (Inline SNI, Offline SNI), CA (CA, TSL CA, CA Group), Intermediate CA (Intermediate CA, Intermediate CA Group), CRL (CRL, CRL Group), Certificate Verify (Certificate Verify, Server Certificate Verify), OCSP (OCSP Stapling, OCSP Responder, OCSP Signing Certificates), Public Key Pinning
SSL Ciphers SSL Ciphers (Predefined, Custom)
Global Global Allow List (Predefined Global Allow List, Custom Global Allow List), Policy Based Allow List, Data Type (Data Type, Custom Data Type), URL Replacer (URL Replacer Policy, URL Replacer Rule)
X-Forwarded-For X-Forwarded-For
IP Group IP Group

On FortiWeb 8.0.6 the menu also has Certificates → ACME and Global → Bot Public Keys. Any other build shows what its own GUI has.

ℹ️Note — Virtual IP and Sign CA are not here

FortiWeb files Virtual IP under Network, so it is at FortiWeb → Network → Virtual IP. Sign CA has no page in FortiWeb's GUI: it is listed under FortiWeb → Not in GUI, but in CLI → System (see Not in GUI, but in CLI).

Requirements#

  • A FortiWeb appliance registered in SATOM and selected as the current device (device picker or Architecture map). With no device selected, the FortiWeb group holds only Server Policy.
  • A GUI layout for the device's build. The layouts arrive with the knowledge packs; until one is imported the Server Objects group is not drawn, and the old page at /server-objects/<id> still opens from a bookmark.
  • A local copy of the device configuration. A device that has never been synchronised shows No objects of this type cached for <device>. A configuration sync fills the SATOM cache. until you refresh it.

Permissions#

Action Who can do it
Open the pages, browse lists, open an object read-only protection.view
Refresh from the device (⟳) Users with a configuration-write permission (it runs a full device sync)
Create New, Save in a dialog, Clone, Delete, row edits Users with a configuration-write permission, typically network.edit or network.apply
Import a certificate Same configuration-write permission
Save as template operations.template_save

The write actions are gated by the legacy config_write check. Any of these granular permissions grants it: network.edit, network.apply, protection.edit, protection.apply, operations.apply, operations.template_save, operations.template_apply, operations.template_approve, appliances.edit, appliances.apply. The Operator and Administrator system profiles have it; Viewer does not.

🔑Permission — What a user without write permission sees

The ⟳ refresh, Clone, Delete and Import buttons are hidden, and Edit reads View: the dialog opens for reading. A save sent anyway is refused with HTTP 403.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the ⟳ refresh now needs a configuration-write permission, like the refresh of Web Protection and the configuration sections, and write buttons are hidden from users who cannot use them.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 3.1.0: Server Objects is a group of FortiWeb's own menu, under FortiWeb → Server Objects; the Loadbalancer → Server Objects menu is gone. Its pages open at /workspace/<id>/fwgui/<page> in FortiWeb's layout, and an old /server-objects/ address redirects to the page that draws the same objects. New <type> became FortiWeb's Create New, the row buttons became Edit, Clone and Delete on the selected row, and the Classic view button is gone.

How to use#

Browse objects#

  1. Select a FortiWeb device.
  2. In the sidebar open FortiWeb → Server Objects and pick an entry, for example Server → Server Pool. FortiWeb → All pages shows the same menu as a grid.
  3. The breadcrumb shows FortiWeb's menu path (FortiWeb / Server Objects / Server / Server Pool) and the header the device and its firmware. Type in Search to narrow the rows; the toolbar counts N objects.
  4. If the page has tabs (for example CA | TSL CA | CA Group), click a tab to switch collection.
  5. Click a row to select it. Double-click it, press Enter or click Edit to open it.

Refresh from the device#

The cache badge in the toolbar says when SATOM's copy was taken. Click the ⟳ button next to it (Pull live config from the device, needs a configuration-write permission) to synchronise the whole device. A flash message reports the result: Refreshed from <device>: <detail>.

Create an object#

  1. Click Create New. Where FortiWeb's menu offers several kinds, pick one.
  2. FortiWeb's dialog opens with FortiWeb's defaults. Enter the Name and the fields; inline tables (pool members, rules…) take rows with their own Create New.
  3. Click Save, check Review the change, then click Apply to <device> (or Back to the form).

On a page where FortiWeb's layout has no Create New (for example CA Group or CRL), Create New opens the object editor in create mode instead.

Edit an object#

Select the row and click Edit (or double-click it). Every save shows Review the change first and is written only after Apply to <device>. The pencil beside a reference selector opens the selected object in a panel stacked over the dialog; Esc closes it.

Clone an object#

  1. Select the row and click Clone.
  2. Enter the new name (default <name>-copy).
  3. Confirm the dry run, which names the sub-table rows that come along. The toast reads Cloned and the list reloads.

Delete an object#

  1. Select the row and click Delete.
  2. Confirm the first prompt. SATOM sends a dry-run and shows DRY-RUN DELETE <path> — nothing has been removed yet.
  3. Confirm Apply this delete to the device now? to delete it. A Deleted toast appears and the list reloads.

SATOM refuses the delete while other objects still reference the object; see Troubleshooting.

Import certificate material#

The REST API cannot create objects in the Local, CA, Intermediate CA and XML Certificate certificate stores. Their pages add Import to the toolbar (and Generate on Local).

  1. Open the certificate page, for example Server Objects → Certificates → Local, and click Import.
  2. Fill in Name on the appliance, paste Certificate (PEM) and, where the store needs it, the private key (or the Secret key for XML client certificates) and Key passphrase (only if encrypted).
  3. Click Import to .

SATOM parses the certificate, proves the key belongs to it before anything is sent, uploads the pair over SSH, then reads the store back and only reports success if the device lists the new name. On success you return to the list with Imported <name> into <store> on <device>.

💡Tip — Generate instead of importing

On the Local tab, Generate opens the Certificate Manager, where the key is created in SATOM, signed by your ADCS/ACME and tracked for renewal. Or let the appliance run ACME itself under Let's Encrypt — then the key never leaves the box, and SATOM cannot renew or clone it.

Configuration#

Import form fields:

Field Description Required Example
Name on the appliance Name the certificate is stored under. Letters, digits, ., -, _; at most 63 characters. Yes wildcard-example-com
Certificate (PEM) The leaf certificate. If you paste a full chain, SATOM warns that FortiWeb wants the leaf here and the issuers in Intermediate CA. Yes -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----…
Private key / Secret key (PEM) Shown only for stores that hold a key (Local, Sign CA, XML Server Certificate, XML Client Certificate). Yes, when shown -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----…
Key passphrase (only if encrypted) Shown for Local, Sign CA and XML Server Certificate. Only for an encrypted key —

Example#

🧪Example — Add a member pool for a new application on fweb-01

  1. Select fweb-01, open FortiWeb → Server Objects → Server → Server Pool.
  2. Click Create New, name the pool pool-shop, click Save, then Apply to fweb-01. pool-shop is listed when the page reloads.
  3. Select pool-shop and click Edit. In the members table, use Create New to add 192.0.2.10 and 192.0.2.11; each row is saved through Review the change → Apply to fweb-01.

Result#

  • Every applied create, update or delete is written to the device through SATOM's audited write path: a change-history record and an audit entry (config.create, config.update, config.delete).
  • An applied update or delete also updates SATOM's local copy of that object, so the list does not have to wait for the next full sync.
  • A certificate import is audited as server_objects.import.
  • A refresh records a synchronisation run for the device.

Troubleshooting#

"Forbidden"#

Possible causes - Your profile has no configuration-write permission.

Solution 1. Ask an administrator to add network.edit (or another key listed in Permissions) to your profile.

Verification - Save now shows Review the change instead of Forbidden.

"refusing to delete "": it is referenced by N object(s) — …"#

Possible causes - Another object (a policy, profile or rule) still names the object.

Solution 1. Open each object named in the message and remove the reference. 2. Delete again.

Verification - The dry-run step shows DRY-RUN DELETE … instead of the refusal.

"No objects of this type cached for . A configuration sync fills the SATOM cache."#

Possible causes - The device has never been synchronised, or the type has no objects.

Solution 1. Click ⟳ in the toolbar. Without a configuration-write permission the button is hidden; ask an operator to refresh the device.

Verification - The cache badge shows the time of the refresh and the counter updates.

A Server Objects page is missing from the menu#

Possible causes - The device's build has no such page in FortiWeb's GUI, or no GUI layout for the build has been imported yet (with no layout, the FortiWeb group holds only Server Policy). - A collection that no measured page draws has no menu entry until its page is measured and arrives in a knowledge pack.

Solution 1. Check that the knowledge packs are up to date. 2. A bookmark to the old page (/server-objects/<id>?type=<object type>) still opens it while no measured page draws that collection.

"Refresh failed: …" or "Refreshed from : device refused the sweep …"#

Possible causes - The device is unreachable, its credentials are wrong, or it is license-locked. The previous local copy is kept.

Solution 1. Check the appliance's connectivity and credentials (see Appliances). 2. Refresh again.

Verification - The flash message is green and the freshness badge updates.

Import: "this private key does NOT belong to this certificate (public keys differ) — refusing to upload the pair"#

Possible causes - The key was generated for a different certificate.

Solution 1. Paste the private key that matches the certificate.

Verification - The import succeeds and the summary shows Subject, Issuer and Expires.

Import: "the private key is encrypted — enter its passphrase"#

Solution 1. Fill in Key passphrase (only if encrypted) and submit again.

Import: " does not list back after the import — treat it as NOT imported"#

Possible causes - The CLI accepted the block but the store does not contain the entry.

Solution 1. Check the PEM content (it must not be empty) and the name, then import again.

Verification - After the import, the name appears in the store's list.

Other import messages#

  • no PEM certificate found in the certificate box — paste a PEM block with BEGIN CERTIFICATE/END CERTIFICATE lines.
  • <store> needs its private key (or secret key) — the store holds a key; paste it.
  • invalid certificate name … — use letters, digits, '.', '-', '_' (<=63) — rename the certificate.

Advanced#

Advanced Where the data comes from

The menu is FortiWeb's own, measured on real firmware builds and delivered by the knowledge packs. Each page uses the layout of the device's exact build, else the same version, else the same train, else the closest older train; the page header says which build the layout comes from. When the device's own build was measured, a page that only another build's menu has is left out. The menu is cached for 60 seconds per product and build.

List rows come from the local configuration store (DB-first); the device is contacted only by the refresh button, the Automation device sync, the live read of predefined entries, and the dialogs' own reads and writes.

An old /server-objects/<id>?type=<object type> address redirects to the measured page that draws the same collection; ?classic=1 keeps the old page. /server-objects/ and its per-device pages belong to the FortiWeb ADOM. Opening one from the Global ADOM switches that browser tab to the FortiWeb ADOM, and opening a device's page makes it the selected device.

Advanced Why certificates use Import

A REST create in those stores is refused by FortiWeb (-7721) even with a valid PEM, so SATOM never offers New there and the create endpoint refuses them with <store> material cannot be created over the REST API — import it over SSH (Server Objects → <store> → Import). The SSH session used for the import can only emit a config system certificate <table> block.

#server objects#virtual server#server pool#health check#persistence#content routing#protected hostnames#service#certificates#ssl ciphers#ip group#x-forwarded-for#import certificate
